entry.description: Analysis of a Conforming Finite Element Method for Second-Harmonic Generation Scattering. The paper reports that under stated small-data conditions, the paper proves existence and uniqueness for continuous and conforming-FE discrete second-harmonic-generation scattering solutions, quasi-optimal H1 error estimates, fixed-point convergence, and a combined discretization/iteration error bound. The paper attributes this AI role: Potentially material proof-strategy and proof-critique assistance; outputs were treated as unverified suggestions. Published provisionally because further checking is required: identify adopted ChatGPT proof strategies, independently check the nonlinear Céa argument and small-data constants, and separate theorem support from illustrative numerics. Keep provisional, unreviewed, and no Superhuman override.

entry.description: Weight decomposition for toroidal abelian fibrations. The paper reports that for torus-rank-at-most-one degenerations of principally polarized abelian varieties, the paper computes the unit-section class, constructs a relative Chow-motive weight decomposition (including the stated Corti–Hanamura case), and determines the tautological ring. The paper attributes this AI role: Potentially material combinatorial assistance is acknowledged but not mapped to any of the three main theorem packages. Published provisionally because further checking is required: identify the LLM-handled combinatorics, independently verify the unit-section formula, motive decomposition/Corti–Hanamura correspondence, and tautological-ring computation, and assess whether one package should be split editorially. Keep provisional, unreviewed, and no Superhuman override.

entry.description: Hermitian curvature flow and HKT geometry. On the standard quaternionic Hopf surface, Theorem 1.6 constructs a sequence of nonhomogeneous HKT–Einstein metrics e^{u_k}g_Hopf with ||u_k||_{C⁰}→∞, giving the first such nonhomogeneous examples and a divergent sequence. The authors attribute this AI role: The construction behind the metrics was suggested by ChatGPT; after Daniele Angella pointed it out, the authors used further ChatGPT consultation to develop a complete proof.

entry.description: AI-Assisted Discovery and Construction of a Counterexample to the Convergence of Three-Block ADMM with the Identity Matrix as its Third Constraint Block. Codex/GPT-5.6 produced an explicit rational three-block ADMM instance with bounded nonconvergent orbit of exact period 66. The authors attribute this AI role: The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), as a landmark algorithm, has attracted tremendous research attention and extensive practical applications over the past two decades [3]. It is well known that, although the two-block ADMM enjoys well-established theoretical convergence guarantees, its direct extension to the three-block case may fail to converge, as demonstrated by existing counterexamples [5].…

entry.description: Near diagonal additive energy bound for points on algebraic surfaces. If F∈R[x,y,z] is irreducible of degree at least 2 and a finite X⊂Z(F) has uniformly bounded concentration on affine lines, then E(X)≪_{deg F,ε}|X|^{2+ε}; more generally the theorem quantifies the sharp loss from line concentration. The authors attribute this AI role: GPT-5.6 was asked to study the unit-sphere case using the authors' earlier ideas and polynomial partitioning. Its observation that the near-diagonal theorem holds for the sphere led the authors to recognize and prove the general line-concentration formulation.

entry.description: Universal Volume Growth Bounds from Positive Intermediate Curvature. If a complete connected n-manifold has Ricci curvature at least -delta^2 and (m+1)-intermediate curvature at least 1, then delta R below a dimension-dependent threshold implies Vol B_R(p) at most C(n,m)R^m. In particular, nonnegative Ricci and scalar curvature at least 1 give Gromov's conjectured codimension-two volume-growth estimate. The authors attribute this AI role: This work made substantial use of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol with Ultra reasoning effort and Codex. GPT proposed the central inductive procedure based on the Hodge obstruction and rank improvement behind the proof of Corollary 1.3. I formulated and guided the problem, suggested relevant strategies and literature, and, following the suggested proof strategy of Corollary 1.3, developed this note. I emphasize that the proof below is quite different from the original argument suggested by GPT.…

entry.description: Zero-Sum Cycles in Regular Digraphs. The paper reports that for Γ-labeled simple loopless d-regular digraphs, the paper proves a zero-sum cycle for d≥e³(k−1), Ω(d/k) vertex-disjoint cycles, and Ω(d²/k) edge-disjoint cycles when d≥50k; all orders are claimed asymptotically optimal and extend to stated Eulerian degree conditions. The paper attributes this AI role: Direct proof-development assistance, but model-generated versus author-generated steps are unspecified. Published provisionally because further checking is required: map ChatGPT's role to the determinant–permanent proof, independently verify all three bounds and sharpness constructions, and distinguish the proved e³ threshold from the conjecturally sharp |Γ|+1 threshold. Keep provisional, unreviewed, and no Superhuman override.

entry.description: Perfect Divisibility, Linear Divisibility and Chair-Free Graphs. For every nonnegative t, the join of the Paley graph P(17) with K_t obeys chi(H) <= binomial(omega(H)+1,2) for every induced subgraph H but is not perfectly divisible, giving an infinite counterexample family. The AI-found P(17) witness, rather than the separately obtained chair-free theorem, is the credited result. The authors attribute this AI role: We thank Songling Shan for an insightful question that led us to modify the definition of (k,ℓ)(k,\ell)-linear divisibility to take into account the number of parts in the decomposition. The Paley graph P⁡(17)P(17) was identified during exploratory use of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and was subsequently verified by the authors. OpenAI’s ChatGPT was also used for language polishing and for generating the Python code used in the computational verification.…

entry.description: On the Positivity of the Products of Positive Primitive Forms. entry.description: A Ten-Vertex Counterexample to a Conjecture on Unstable Graphs. Mizzi conjectured that every nontrivially unstable graph contains cycles C_k and C_{2k} for some odd k. We give a connected, nonbipartite, vertex-determining counterexample on ten vertices. Its instability is certified by an explicit nontrivial two-fold automorphism, and its complete set of simple-cycle lengths is {5,5,6}. The authors attribute this AI role: A dependency-free exact verifier reconstructs the graph from (2), checks all ten neighbourhood identities, checks the induced automorphism of the canonical double cover, and enumerates every simple cycle. The example, verifier, and drafting were developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. The proof above is self-contained, and the author takes responsibility for all claims.

entry.description: Rigidity and non-rigidity of the stable norm on $T^n$. For any unit-volume flat metric g₀ on T³, Theorem 1.4 constructs a smooth family g(s) starting at g₀ such that g(s) is nonflat for s>0, the stable norm on H₂(T³,R) stays fixed, and vol_{g(s)}(T³) decreases to 0. entry.description: Five-Term and Higher Congruences Involving Arbitrary Sets and Short Intervals Modulo a Prime. For five balanced variables of common size N, the stated additive congruence has the expected asymptotic uniformly in λ once N>p^(14/29+ε); for every fixed r≥5 the paper gives sub-square-root thresholds, including 8/17 for r=6 and α_r=1/3+4/(9√r)+O(r^−1). The authors attribute this AI role: Parts of the proof strategy for Theorem 1.1 were developed with partial inspiration from ChatGPT 5.5 discussions; AI also assisted computations, algebraic manipulations, and verification, while the author independently checked the final manuscript.

entry.description: Optimal Lower Bounds for Networked Information Aggregation. For networked aggregation with D transmitted bits, the worst-case mean-squared error is Omega(1/sqrt(D)), matching the upper bound; the lower-bound method extends to the stated convex-loss settings, including logistic loss. The authors attribute this AI role: We thank Aaron Roth and Michael Kearns for helpful discussions. Additionally, GPT 5.6 was used to discover the reference (Li and Duan 1989), shorten lengthy algebra in the generating function proof of Lemma 4.5, discover the elementary proof of Lemma B.1 by bounding the cosh\cosh function, and discover other losses that our argument applies to in Section 5.3.

entry.description: The Holonomy of Optimal Mass Transport: The Smooth Case. On every smooth n-dimensional boundaryless Riemannian manifold, any vector field is a linear combination of at most max{6,6n−3} depth-one Lie brackets of gradient fields; on compact connected manifolds this implies density of the group generated by diffeomorphic optimal-transport maps in Diff₀. The authors attribute this AI role: The absorption identity (12), which the authors call key to the main result and apparently novel, was produced in interaction with Claude Fable 5; the authors verified its mathematical details.

entry.description: A proof of Bickle's conjecture on collapsible graphs. A graph $G$ is said to be $k$-collapsible if $G$ has minimum degree $k$ and every non-null proper induced subgraph of $G$ has minimum degree less than $k.$ In 2018, Bickle conjectured that the minimum number of vertices of degree $k$ in a $k$-collapsible graph of order $n$ with $k\ge 3$ is ${\rm max}\{\lceil 2n/(2k-1)\rceil,\, k^2-k-2-(k-3)n\}.$ We prove this conjecture. The authors attribute this AI role: ChatGPT was used to assist in developing and checking the constructions and proofs. The author independently verified all mathematical arguments, wrote the paper, and takes full responsibility for its content.

entry.description: Adjoint reductions of tangent bundles of spheres. The paper reports: If $d=\dim G$ and $r=\operatorname{rank} G$, we show that the adjoint map $\operatorname{Ad}\colon G\longrightarrow \mathrm{SO}(d)$ is homotopic, as an ordinary map, to one with values in $\mathrm{SO}(d-r+1)$. It follows that every vector bundle over a sphere associated to a principal $G$-bundle via the adjoint representation admits $r-1$ linearly independent sections. Combined with Adams's theorem on vector fields on spheres, this gives the necessary condition $r\le ρ(d+1)$ for an adjoint reduction of $TS^d$. The primary paper directly acknowledges GPT-5.6, ChatGPT for proof development and mathematical exploration, code, computation, or algebraic checking, literature and reference work, writing and exposition. It assigns final checking, decisions, or responsibility to the human author team.
entry.anchor_claim: We study reductions of the tangent bundle of $S^{\dim G}$ through the adjoint representation of a compact connected Lie group $G$. If $d=\dim G$ and $r=\operatorname{rank} G$, we show that the adjoint map $\operatorname{Ad}\colon G\longrightarrow \mathrm{SO}(d)$ is homotopic, as an ordinary map, to one with values in $\mathrm{SO}(d-r+1)$. It follows that every vector bundle over a sphere associated to a principal $G$-bundle via the adjoint representation admits $r-1$ linearly independent sections. Combined with Adams's theorem on vector fields on spheres, this gives the necessary condition $r\le ρ(d+1)$ for an adjoint reduction of $TS^d$. In particular, no such reduction exists for a non-trivial compact connected group, simple or not, of dimension $d>1$ with $d\not\equiv3\pmod4$. As an application, this excludes the adjoint $E_7$-reduction of $TS^{133}$ that is the exceptional branch in the structure-group argument of Bor, Hernández-Lamoneda, Jiménez-Desantiago and Montejano for Banach's isometric subspace problem.

Combined with Adams's theorem on vector fields on spheres, this gives the necessary condition $r\le ρ(d+1)$ for an adjoint reduction of $TS^d$. In particular, no such reduction exists for a non-trivial compact connected group, simple or not, of dimension $d>1$ with $d\not\equiv3\pmod4$. As an application, this excludes the adjoint $E_7$-reduction of $TS^{133}$ that is the exceptional branch in the structure-group argument of Bor, Hernández-Lamoneda, Jiménez-Desantiago and Montejano for Banach's isometric subspace problem.

entry.description: A finite forbidden family with superlinear surplus and no three-factor product extremizers. The paper reports: We construct a fixed finite family $\mathcal L$ of ordinary forbidden subgraphs with $p(\mathcal L)=3$ and a constant $c>0$ such that $$ex(n,\mathcal L)>t_3(n)+cn^{3/2}$$ at every sufficiently large order. Nevertheless, the complement of every sufficiently large $\mathcal L$-extremal graph has at most two connected components. In particular, no such extremal graph is a complete join of three graphs of positive order. This gives a negative answer to a natural existence-only question motivated by the Simonovits Product Conjecture, in which one asks only for one product extremizer at each sufficiently large order. entry.description: Exact MMS Allocations under Personalized Bivalued Valuations: Goods and Chores. The paper reports: The maximin share (MMS) is a central fairness benchmark for allocating indivisible goods and chores. We study additive valuations in the personalized bivalued setting, where each agent assigns one of two agent-specific values to every item. Whether exact MMS allocations always exist in this setting has remained a major open question, as highlighted by Ebadian, Peters, and Shah and by Garg, Huang, and Segal-Halevi. The paper reports: We prove that the volume of a compact connected Kähler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature at least 2 is bounded above by the volume of the Fubini-Study metric of constant holomorphic sectional curvature 2 on the complex projective space of the same dimension. Moreover equality holds if and only if the manifold is biholomorphically isometric to complex projective space. This answers a question posed by Xiong and Yang. entry.anchor_claim: We prove that the volume of a compact connected Kähler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature at least 2 is bounded above by the volume of the Fubini-Study metric of constant holomorphic sectional curvature 2 on the complex projective space of the same dimension. Moreover equality holds if and only if the manifold is biholomorphically isometric to complex projective space. This answers a question posed by Xiong and Yang. Our approach also yields a different proof of Zhang's sharp volume estimate and Liu's rigidity theorem for compact Kähler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature. In fact, our main result states that the same sharp volume estimate holds under a new curvature positivity condition (mean RC curvature positivity), which is implied by both positive Ricci curvature and positive holomorphic sectional curvature. challengeContext.anchorClaim: We prove that the volume of a compact connected Kähler manifold with holomorphic sectional curvature at least 2 is bounded above by the volume of the Fubini-Study metric of constant holomorphic sectional curvature 2 on the complex projective space of the same dimension. Moreover equality holds if and only if the manifold is biholomorphically isometric to complex projective space. This answers a question posed by Xiong and Yang. Our approach also yields a different proof of Zhang's sharp volume estimate and Liu's rigidity theorem for compact Kähler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature. In fact, our main result states that the same sharp volume estimate holds under a new curvature positivity condition (mean RC curvature positivity), which is implied by both positive Ricci curvature and positive holomorphic sectional curvature. The definition of this condition was inspired by the work of Yang. The proofs in this paper are due to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, and the paper is merely an exposition of its output. The proofs has been verified by the authors and they take full responsibility for any errors.

entry.description: Bounded independence for the inverse star discrepancy. The paper reports: We give a random-bit-efficient construction for the inverse star discrepancy. For every fixed $u\in(0,1)$, $k$-wise independent uniform points $\boldsymbol{X}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{X}_N$ with $k=O(d(1+\log(1+N/d)))$ satisfy the Monte Carlo bound $D_N^*(\boldsymbol{X}_1,\ldots,\boldsymbol{X}_N) =O(\sqrt{d/N})$ with probability at least $u$. Consequently, $N=O(d\varepsilon^{-2})$ and $k=O(d(1+\log\varepsilon^{-1}))$ suffice to attain discrepancy at most $\varepsilon$. The proof isolates the finitely many moments required by a chaining argument and gives explicit constants. A random vector-valued polynomial over a finite field realizes the required bounded independence on a grid using $O(d^2(1+\log(1+N/d))\log N)$ random bits, rather than the $Θ(dN\log(dN))$ bits used by independent grid sampling. entry.description: A nonabelian Brunn-Minkowski inequality II. The paper reports: We prove that every unimodular locally compact group $G$ of noncompact Lie dimension $n$ satisfies the sharp Brunn--Minkowski inequality \[ μ_G(XY)^{1/n}\geμ_G(X)^{1/n}+μ_G(Y)^{1/n}, \] and establish a general form for arbitrary, possibly nonunimodular, locally compact groups. This fully confirms the nonabelian Brunn--Minkowski conjecture proposed by the present authors and Zhang. As an application, we obtain an isoperimetric inequality on symmetric spaces of noncompact type. entry.anchor_claim: The paper reports: Let $I=(0,ρ)$, where $0<ρ\leq\infty$, and let $\mathbb{P}_n(I)$ denote the cone of real positive semidefinite $n\times n$ matrices whose entries belong to $I$. A longstanding problem in matrix theory is to characterize the functions $f: I \to \mathbb{R}$ for which the entrywise calculus $f[A] = (f(a_{ij}))$ preserves positive semidefiniteness for all $A = (a_{ij}) \in \mathbb{P}_n(I)$. We provide an explicit function-theoretic characterization of such preservers via the Euler--Hankel matrix associated to $f$. We begin by providing the characterization for functions $f \in C^{2n-2}(I)$. Writing $\mathcal{E} =x\frac{d}{dx}$ and denoting the Euler--Hankel matrix by $$ \mathcal{H}_n(f;x)=\bigl[\mathcal{E}^{i+j}f(x)\bigr]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}, $$ we prove that $f[-]$ preserves positivity on $\mathbb{P}_n(I)$ if and only if $f^{(k)}(x) \geq0$ for $0\leq k\leq n-1$ and $\mathcal{H}_n(f;x)\succeq 0$ for every $x\in I$. The proof combines Karlin's finite-order criterion for additive Hankel kernels with an extension principle of Khare and Tao. We then show how the smoothness hypothesis can be entirely removed to obtain the same characterization for general functions, where the above conditions are interpreted as inequalities between distributions. We conclude by showing how our results recover the smooth form of Vasudeva's characterization in dimension two, the FitzGerald--Horn critical exponent for power functions, and the characterization of Belton--Guillot--Khare--Putinar of polynomial preservers of degree at most $n$ on $\mathbb{P}_n(I)$. Finally, we extend the Khare--Tao characterization of sums of real powers preserving rank $1$ positive semidefinite matrices to sums of real powers that preserve the full cone $\mathbb{P}_n(I)$.
